newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Napocor sets terms for sales contracts.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Napocor sets terms for sales contracts.

text.p: The state-run National Power Corp (Napocor) board has approved the terms of reference (TOR) for its future long-term power sales contracts, a Napocor official said on Wednesday.
Napocor vice-president Asisclo Gonzaga said the terms were made attractive to buyers in the face of competition from independent power producers.

He said the terms will include a guarantee from the power firm that it will not increase its generation charges for the duration of the contract. The generation charges are exclusive of fuel and foreign exchange costs.
Gonzaga added that the board also approved a provision allowing for the purchase of additional load other than the contracted power.
"This is in preparation for our privatisation, where before our contracts were somewhat monopolistic in view, now we are veering away from that," said Gonzaga.
Napocor has started negotiating long-term sales contracts with its customers.
Prior to the long-term sales contract scheme, Napocor was involved in short-term contracts of about three years.
The firm, the biggest electricity producer in the Philippines, is planning to create subsidiaries and spin them off as part of the government's privatisation plans.
